meta.title: Coaster Life
meta.subtitle: Gold Coast's life design: what a Coaster needs, what they can become, and the world they live it in.
meta.notes: A Coaster is anyone living in Gold Coast. Three systems work together: needs and behaviour (what does the Coaster need now?), life progression (what can the Coaster become, achieve, or reach over time?), and the world (where, and with whom, do they live it?). The game today is one young woman's hustle in town; this is where a Coaster comes from, and where they can go.

principles.name: Needs pull, the world offers
principles.text: Every action says what it gives (+25 hunger) and takes (−20 hygiene). The Coaster weighs each one by how badly they need it, the way The Sims' objects advertise.

principles.name: Survive first, then belong, then rise
principles.text: Hunger, thirst, sleep and the toilet come first. Company, fun and belonging count for more once the body is safe; hope and respect most of all when the rest is in place.

principles.name: Money never opens everything
principles.text: Every step also asks for something money can't buy: a skill, an education, a relationship, a reputation, or a choice. The board warns you when money alone opens a step.

principles.name: Every lock says how to open it
principles.text: Nothing is hidden. Each step lists exactly what it takes, so the player always knows what to work on next.

principles.name: Hard, but never hopeless
principles.text: Life starts hard (food from the rubbish, a market table for a roof), but nothing is lost for good, and kindness, faith and community are always a way up.

principles.name: Ghana is the content
principles.text: Kenkey and waakye, trotros, susu, dumsor, Free SHS, apprenticeships and freedom ceremonies, knocking, landguards and funerals: they are the mechanics, not decoration.

principles.name: Follow the player's lead
principles.text: A Coaster looks after their own needs, but never undoes the player's choices: they won't quit school, leave a partner or skip work by themselves.

howToEdit: A branch is a step in 'opportunities'. Add one with a new id, and put the id of the step it grows from in its 'after'.
'after' lists the steps that must come first: all of them, or any one if 'afterAny' is true. Leave it empty and the step opens when the Coaster reaches its life stage.

'requires' says what a step takes. Each has a 'kind' (choices, education, skills, relationships, reputation or resources) and a 'what'. Give every step at least one kind that isn't resources: money alone never opens anything.
An action's 'requires' is the id of the step that opens it, like 'taken_in' opening 'Sleep on a mat'. Its 'needs' are what it gives (+) and takes (−); 'earns' is [least, most] in cedis.

An action's 'hours' (like "07:00 to 12:00") and 'days' (mon to sun) say when it can happen; 'until' names the step after which the Coaster stops doing it (no more gutter once someone takes you in). A routine line's 'actions' are what it pulls towards at that time.
Remove a branch by deleting its step, and any steps that only come after it. The board's Remove button does this, and takes out the links to it too.

'jobs' is the build plan: each job brings parts of the design into the game, listed in its 'uses' (needs, steps, actions, places, coasters, events, achievements, skills, moodlets). Its order is the order to build them; its number is its name.

'tutorial' holds the lessons. 'when' is one of: start, after:<lesson>, need below:<need> <number>, first:<something happening>, arrive:<place>, time:<HH:MM>, day:<number>, money above:<cedis>, money below:<cedis>. 'point' is place:<place> or ui:<part of the screen>. 'doneWhen' is what ticks it off ('got it' means a button).

dimensions.name: Choices
dimensions.text: The paths the Coaster commits to: school or the market, faith, love, staying or leaving.

dimensions.name: Education
dimensions.text: School and certificates: basic school, the BECE, Free SHS, the WASSCE, a trade's freedom, a course, a degree.

dimensions.name: Skills
dimensions.text: What the Coaster can do, from 0 to 10: street smarts, trading, sewing, football, reading…

dimensions.name: Relationships
dimensions.text: Who knows them, trusts them, and vouches for them: a guardian, a master, friends, a partner, the family, the elders.

dimensions.name: Reputation
dimensions.text: Their name in each circle: the market, the street, the church or mosque, the school, the family, the town.

dimensions.name: Resources
dimensions.text: Cedis, things (a head pan, a sewing machine), papers (a birth certificate, a Ghana Card) and property (a stall, land, a house).

lifeStages.name: Toddler
lifeStages.text: Small, but already surviving. Needs come fast, and the market floor is the whole world.

lifeStages.name: Child
lifeStages.text: Old enough to help, to hawk, or to learn. Someone to look after them changes everything.

lifeStages.name: Teen
lifeStages.text: Strong enough to carry loads, old enough to choose: school, a trade, or the street.

lifeStages.name: Young adult
lifeStages.text: Papers, money, love, and the first big bets.

lifeStages.name: Adult
lifeStages.text: Building: a business, a house, a family, a name.

lifeStages.name: Elder
lifeStages.text: People come for advice. What they built outlives them.

needTiers.name: Survival
needTiers.text: The body comes first. These get urgent fast.

needTiers.name: Safety and comfort
needTiers.text: Being clean, and somewhere safe to lay your head.

needTiers.name: Heart
needTiers.text: People and joy. They count for more once the body is looked after.

needTiers.name: Spirit
needTiers.text: Hope and dignity. Slow to fall, slow to rise, and they colour every choice.

needs.name: Hunger
needs.text: Food: kenkey and fish, waakye, a plate at the chop bar, or whatever a hungry child can find.
needs.whenLow: Below 25 the Coaster can think of nothing else. At 0, energy drains fast and health starts to fall.

needs.name: Thirst
needs.text: Water: a sachet of pure water, the standpipe, a kind seller's cup. In the Harmattan it goes faster.
needs.whenLow: In the heat, thirst comes before hunger. At 0, health falls quickly.

needs.name: Energy
needs.text: Sleep and rest: under a market table, on a station bench, on a mat, or one day in a bed of your own.
needs.whenLow: Tired Coasters work slowly and make mistakes. At 0 they fall asleep wherever they are.

needs.name: Bladder
needs.text: The public toilet costs a coin. The gutter costs your dignity.
needs.whenLow: At 0, an accident: hygiene and respect drop.

needs.name: Health
needs.text: Malaria, cholera and fever come from mosquitoes, bad water and bad food. The chemist, the nurse and an NHIS card bring it back.
needs.whenLow: Sick Coasters can't work or learn, and need care. It falls through risks and events, not the clock.

needs.name: Hygiene
needs.text: A bucket bath, the bathhouse, the sea, clean clothes off the line.
needs.whenLow: People keep their distance: friendships, work and respect all suffer.

needs.name: Safety
needs.text: A safe place to sleep, and someone who has your back: a kind seller nearby, a guardian's room, a door that locks.
needs.whenLow: Afraid: the Coaster sleeps badly, and either avoids every risk or takes the wrong ones.

needs.name: Company
needs.text: Talking, gisting, playing, being known by name.
needs.whenLow: Lonely: the mood sinks, and the Coaster looks for any company, even bad company.

needs.name: Fun
needs.text: Ampe, football, music, a Black Stars match at the viewing centre, the songs at church.
needs.whenLow: Bored and restless: learning and work go slower.

needs.name: Belonging
needs.text: Someone who calls you their own: a guardian, a church family, a partner, children, the abusua.
needs.whenLow: Alone in the world: hope drains, and every setback feels bigger.

needs.name: Hope
needs.text: Faith, dreams and small wins. Hope keeps a Coaster trying.
needs.whenLow: Giving up: fewer choices appear, and risky shortcuts start to look good.

needs.name: Respect
needs.text: Being treated with dignity. It comes from honest work, helping others, and how people see you.
needs.whenLow: Ashamed: the Coaster avoids people and accepts less than they deserve.

traits.name: Hustler
traits.text: Always finding a way to make a coin.
traits.effects: Earns 20% more from work; energy falls 10% faster.

traits.name: Sweet mouth
traits.text: Can talk almost anyone into almost anything.
traits.effects: Relationships grow 25% faster; better odds when talking their way out.
traits.motive: Be liked by everyone in the room.

traits.name: Book long
traits.text: Loves to learn. Reads anything, even the newspaper the kelewele comes wrapped in.
traits.effects: Education and reading grow 25% faster; reading is fun for them.

traits.name: Prayerful
traits.text: Faith first: church or mosque every week, and a prayer before every meal.
traits.effects: Hope falls half as fast; more belonging from services.

traits.name: Street smart
traits.text: Knows every shortcut, every trick, every danger.
traits.effects: Safety falls slower at night; better odds in street events.

traits.name: Generous
traits.text: Shares the last piece of bread.
traits.effects: Relationships and reputation grow faster; money goes faster too.
traits.motive: Make sure nobody near them is hungry.

traits.name: Humble
traits.text: Never shows off, and greets every elder properly.
traits.effects: Elders trust them sooner; respect grows 10% faster.
traits.motive: Be thought of as well brought up.

traits.name: Hot temper
traits.text: Quick to fight, quick to forgive.
traits.effects: Wins more confrontations; relationships fall faster after a quarrel.
traits.motive: Never let anyone look down on them.

traits.name: Born footballer
traits.text: A ball at their feet since they could walk.
traits.effects: Football grows 50% faster; any game is fun.

traits.name: Ambitious
traits.text: Dreams big: a house, a car, maybe abroad.
traits.effects: Every step forward lifts hope; big goals show up sooner.

traits.name: Shy
traits.text: Quiet in a crowd, loyal in private.
traits.effects: Company falls slower; meeting strangers is harder.
traits.motive: A few close friends, not a crowd.

traits.name: Joker
traits.effects: Lifts the fun of people nearby; company grows faster.

traits.name: Neat
traits.text: Ironed clothes, swept floor, everything in its place.
traits.effects: Hygiene matters more to them; better at sewing and cooking.

decisionModel.text: How a Coaster decides by themselves. Every action says what it gives and takes. The Coaster weighs each gain by how badly they need it (urgent needs climb steeply as they fall, and the heart and spirit count for more once the body is fed), adds a little for what their personality likes, leaves out what they can't do yet, then picks one of the best three at random, the better ones more often, so they never feel like robots.

explain.pickFromTop: picks at random among this many of the best
explain.curves: how steeply each kind of need gets urgent as it falls (bigger is steeper)
explain.maslowTiers: tiers that count for less while the body is hungry, thirsty or tired
explain.maslowFloor: how much those tiers still count when the body's needs are empty (0 to 1)
explain.lossWeight: how much a loss hurts compared with a gain of the same size
explain.traitLikeBonus: times the score when their personality likes the action
explain.earnWeight: how much earning money counts, when they have little
explain.costWeight: how much spending counts against an action, when they have little
explain.comfortableCedis: at each life stage, money above this stops pulling them to work
explain.sleepDecay: needs fall this much slower while asleep
explain.routineBonus: added to what the Coaster's routine says to do at this time of day
explain.repeatMinutes: doing the same thing again within this many minutes is less appealing…
explain.repeatFactor: …it's worth this share of its score (sleep doesn't count)

schedule.do: Wake under a market table as the sellers arrive
Look for food: leftovers, the rubbish heap, a kind seller
Follow the market women, learning faces
Nap in the shade of the cloth stalls
Play with the other market children
Find a dry, safe place for the night
Sweep the compound, wash the bowls
School (or hawking, if there's no school)
Ampe or football at the park
Eat, then homework under the street light (if there's no dumsor)
Wake in the shared room, or at the station
The market opens: carry loads for Madam Serwaa's customers
Open Madam Adjoa's shop and sweep it
Learn and work: hems, cuts, fittings
Choir practice on Wednesdays, or more sewing
Buy stock at the wholesale market
Family time, and the children's homework
A family meeting, or the palace

relationshipTypes.name: A guardian
relationshipTypes.text: An auntie, a market woman or a church mother who takes the Coaster in.

relationshipTypes.name: Friends
relationshipTypes.text: The market children, school mates, padis.

relationshipTypes.name: A mentor
relationshipTypes.text: A pastor, a teacher, a coach or a businesswoman who believes in them.

relationshipTypes.name: A master
relationshipTypes.text: The tradesperson who teaches an apprentice.

relationshipTypes.name: A boss
relationshipTypes.text: Someone who gives them work: Madam Serwaa, a driver, a car owner.

relationshipTypes.name: Family (abusua)
relationshipTypes.text: Blood, in-laws, and the wider family that comes with marriage.

relationshipTypes.name: Elders and chiefs
relationshipTypes.text: The people who give out land, settle disputes, and bless.

relationshipTypes.name: Customers
relationshipTypes.text: Who comes back to your stall, your kiosk, your trotro.

reputationCircles.name: The market
reputationCircles.text: Honest scales, fair prices, debts paid.

reputationCircles.name: The street
reputationCircles.text: Tough, fair, not to be cheated.

reputationCircles.name: The family
reputationCircles.text: Respectful, responsible, someone the family is proud of.

reputationCircles.name: The town
reputationCircles.text: Known all over Gold Coast: someone people listen to.

resourceTypes.name: Cedis

resourceTypes.name: Things

resourceTypes.name: Papers
resourceTypes.text: A birth certificate, an NHIS card, a Ghana Card, a driver's licence, a passport, a land indenture.

resourceTypes.name: Property

opportunities.name: Alone at the market
opportunities.summary: You're three. Your mother sold tomatoes at Nkabom Market until the fever took her, and nobody knows your father. The market is home now.
unlocks: Survival comes first: food, water, and somewhere safe to sleep

opportunities.name: Learn the market's rhythm
opportunities.summary: Which sellers throw food away at closing, where the shade moves, and when the city guards come.

requires.what: Watch and learn instead of grabbing

opportunities.name: A safe place to sleep
opportunities.summary: Mama Akua lets you sleep under her tomato table: out of the rain, away from the rats, and near someone who'd hear you cry.

opportunities.name: A kind kenkey seller
opportunities.summary: Auntie Akos saves you the ends of the kenkey and calls you 'my small one'.

requires.what: Visit her stall five days in a row
Help carry her bowls instead of stealing

opportunities.name: Counting tomatoes
opportunities.summary: The market women teach you to count by heaping tomatoes in fives.

requires.what: Auntie Akos lets you sit with her
Sit and count instead of running off

opportunities.name: The Saturday feeding programme
opportunities.summary: On Saturday mornings the Methodist church feeds the market children: rice and stew, a Bible story, and a song with actions.

opportunities.name: Taken in by Auntie Akos
opportunities.summary: She has five children already, but one more mouth is no problem, she says. You sleep on a mat in her room at Auntie Adwoa's compound house.
unlocks: A home: safety, and a mat to sleep on
A guardian for school and papers

opportunities.name: Call passengers at the station
opportunities.summary: Shout the destinations for the drivers, and get a coin for every passenger who climbs in.

requires.what: A driver lets you call for him
Spend the day at the station

opportunities.name: A birth certificate
opportunities.summary: At the Births and Deaths Registry, Auntie Akos swears you were born in the rainy season. Now you exist on paper.

requires.what: A guardian to swear for you

opportunities.name: An NHIS card
opportunities.summary: With a National Health Insurance card, the nurse treats your malaria for almost nothing.

opportunities.name: Nkabom M/A Basic School
opportunities.summary: There are no fees, but you still need a uniform, sandals and a pencil. Mrs. Ofori takes you into Class 1.

requires.what: School instead of a full day's work

opportunities.name: Hawk pure water in traffic
opportunities.summary: A cool box of sachets on your head, weaving between the trotros at the junction. A few pesewas profit on every sachet.

requires.what: GH₵ 10 for a bag of sachets

opportunities.name: Run errands for the compound
opportunities.summary: Buy kerosene, carry messages, queue at the standpipe. Small coins, and a lot of trust.
unlocks: A good name in the compound

opportunities.name: Football at the park
opportunities.summary: Stones for goalposts and a ball made of plastic bags.

requires.what: Join the children at the park

opportunities.name: Spotted by a colts coach
opportunities.summary: Coach Kwesi runs the Nkabom Colts. He saw you dribble past three boys.
unlocks: A place in the Nkabom Colts

opportunities.name: The children's choir
opportunities.summary: Sunday school, Christmas carols, and the first time a crowd claps for you.

requires.what: Go to Sunday school every week

opportunities.name: Run with the station boys
opportunities.summary: Calling, loading, and collecting 'tolls' from the drivers. Easy money, until the police come.

opportunities.name: Pass the BECE
opportunities.summary: The Basic Education Certificate Examination at the end of JHS 3. You study under the street light, unless there's dumsor.

opportunities.name: A Free SHS place
opportunities.summary: The computer places you in a boarding school. Fees and food are free; the chop box, the trunk and the provisions are on you.

requires.what: Someone to take you on reporting day

opportunities.name: Apprentice to a master
opportunities.summary: Madam Adjoa, seamstress: you bring the drinks and the fee, and over three years she teaches you everything from hems to kaba styles.

requires.what: A guarantor who vouches for you
Pick a trade: sewing, hair, mechanics, carpentry or welding

unlocks: A master who looks out for you

opportunities.name: Carry loads as a kayayo
opportunities.summary: A head pan from Madam Serwaa's pile, the market at dawn, and loads heavier than you are.

requires.what: Madam Serwaa lets you carry for her customers

opportunities.name: Join a market susu
opportunities.summary: Every evening you give the susu collector a cedi. At the end of the month it all comes back to you, if you trusted the right man.

opportunities.name: Nkabom Colts
opportunities.summary: Training at six in the morning, matches on Saturday. Sometimes scouts from the big clubs come to watch.

opportunities.name: The youth fellowship
opportunities.summary: Choir, drama, football on the church field, and Pastor Mensah, who asks about your future.

opportunities.name: Trotro mate
opportunities.summary: Hang from the sliding door shouting the destination, collect the fares, and count change in a moving bus.

opportunities.name: A room of your own
opportunities.summary: Auntie Adwoa's room at the compound house: a bed, a door that locks, and GH₵140 every Monday.

requires.what: Auntie Adwoa rents it to you
Live on your own in town

opportunities.name: Courtship
opportunities.summary: Walks home after church, phone calls until the credit runs out, and meeting each other's friends.

opportunities.name: The knocking ceremony
opportunities.summary: Kɔkɔɔkɔ: your partner's family comes with drinks to knock on your family's door. Both families must agree.

requires.what: A family to knock on (your guardian counts)

opportunities.name: A Ghana Card
opportunities.summary: The national ID card. The queue at the NIA office starts at five in the morning: bring your birth certificate and your patience.

requires.what: Queue from dawn and lose a day's work

unlocks: A SIM card in your name

opportunities.name: A driver's licence
opportunities.summary: The DVLA test: the road, the rules, and reversing between two poles.

requires.what: Driving school, or years as a mate

opportunities.name: A passport
opportunities.summary: The form wants a guarantor: a teacher, a pastor or a nurse who has known you for years.

requires.what: A guarantor who has known you for years

opportunities.name: Sankofa Training College
opportunities.summary: Short courses that lead to work: teaching, dressmaking, or mobile money. A class a day, a quiz, and a certificate at the end.

requires.what: Pick a course: teaching, dressmaking or mobile money

unlocks: A teaching, dressmaking or mobile money certificate

opportunities.name: Pass the WASSCE
opportunities.summary: The West African Senior School Certificate Examination. Your grades decide which doors open.

opportunities.name: University
opportunities.summary: An admission letter, the fees, and a hostel bed if you're lucky. The Legon dream.

requires.what: Put work aside for four years

opportunities.cost: GH₵ 3,000 a year, or a scholarship

opportunities.name: National Service
opportunities.summary: A year of service after your degree: teaching in a village school, or filing papers at a district office.
unlocks: The service certificate (government jobs ask for it)

opportunities.name: Freedom ceremony
opportunities.summary: In front of both families, your master declares you a qualified seamstress. Drinks, prayers, and a certificate.

requires.what: Drinks and a fowl for the ceremony (GH₵ 200)

unlocks: Apprentices of your own, one day

opportunities.name: Sew for the market women
opportunities.summary: Kaba and slit for the market women, paid by the piece.

requires.what: A freedom certificate, or Sankofa's dressmaking certificate
The cloth sellers trust your work

opportunities.name: A mobile money wallet
opportunities.summary: Mobile money on your own phone: get paid, pay, and save, with no bank.

opportunities.name: Become a MoMo agent
opportunities.summary: A yellow umbrella, a kiosk, and float: other people's money through your hands. Trust is everything.

requires.what: Auntie Dede lets you mind her kiosk first

opportunities.name: Drive a trotro
opportunities.summary: The owner gives you the van; you give him his 'sales' every evening, and what's left is yours.

requires.what: An owner who trusts you with his van

unlocks: One day, a trotro of your own

opportunities.name: Drive for Uber
opportunities.summary: A rented Yaris, a phone on the dashboard, and the app. The weekly payment to the car's owner comes first.

requires.what: A car owner who trusts you
A smartphone and a MoMo wallet

opportunities.cost: GH₵ 900 a week to the owner
unlocks: One day, a car of your own

opportunities.name: A church scholarship
opportunities.summary: The church elders pay your fees, if Pastor Mensah vouches for you.
unlocks: Fees paid at university or college

opportunities.name: An academy trial
opportunities.summary: A scout invites you to a week's trial at a big football academy in the city.

opportunities.name: Station master
opportunities.summary: The drivers' union makes you station master: you decide the queue, settle the fights, and keep the station boys in line.

requires.what: No more tolls: run it straight

opportunities.name: Traditional marriage
opportunities.summary: Kente, drumming, the list read out loud, and everyone eating.

requires.what: The list and the party (GH₵ 5,000 or more)

opportunities.name: A child of your own
opportunities.summary: A naming ceremony on the eighth day. Now someone depends on you.

requires.what: A safe room of your own

unlocks: A child's needs to look after

opportunities.name: Register the land
opportunities.summary: Take the indenture to the Lands Commission, so nobody can sell your plot twice.

requires.what: Knowing the process, or a lawyer friend

unlocks: A bank loan against the land

opportunities.name: The abroad dream
opportunities.summary: Abrokyire: a visa interview and a ticket. Some go and send money home; some come back.

requires.what: Visa fees and proof of funds (GH₵ 15,000 or more)

unlocks: A new chapter abroad (a later expansion)

opportunities.name: Teach at the basic school
opportunities.summary: Mrs. Ofori needs teachers. You know how hard it is to learn when you're hungry.

requires.what: Mrs. Ofori gives you a class

opportunities.name: Headteacher
opportunities.summary: The whole school is yours to run: forty teachers, a leaking roof, and a thousand children.

requires.what: A diploma or degree in education

opportunities.name: Your own sewing shop
opportunities.summary: A signboard with your name on it, two machines, and customers who wait for you.

requires.what: A landlord who rents to you

opportunities.name: Take on apprentices
opportunities.summary: Now you're the master. Your apprentices bring the drinks and learn from you.

requires.what: Your freedom certificate, or years of good work

opportunities.name: Your own market stall
opportunities.summary: A table of your own at Nkabom Market. The market queen has to know you first.

opportunities.name: Open a chop bar
opportunities.summary: Fufu pounding at noon, light soup, and a queue of drivers. Maame Esi will teach you, if you ask her properly.

opportunities.name: An office job
opportunities.summary: A desk, a monthly salary, and a long list of others who applied.

requires.what: A degree and the National Service certificate
Someone inside who puts your name forward
Town: a good name (they'll ask around)

unlocks: A bank loan for land or a car

opportunities.name: Own a trotro
opportunities.summary: A second-hand Sprinter from Tema port, a driver, a mate, and a saying painted on the back.

requires.what: GH₵ 60,000, or a group of owners

unlocks: A seat in the drivers' union

opportunities.name: Buy a plot of land
opportunities.summary: An indenture, a site plan, and maybe landguards who say it's theirs. Ask the chief's people first.

requires.what: A chief or family head who gives it out
Knowing to check the papers first

opportunities.name: Build, block by block
opportunities.summary: The foundation this year, the walls next year, the roof when the susu pays out. Ghanaians build in stages.

requires.what: Blocks and cement, paid in stages

coasters.name: Auntie Akos
coasters.text: Five children of her own and room for one more. Strict about chores, soft about food.
coasters.line: Come, my small one. Have you eaten?
coasters.routine: At her stall from 06:00; church every Sunday.

coasters.name: Mama Akua
coasters.text: Says little, sees everything. She knew your mother.
coasters.line: Sit here, out of the sun.
coasters.routine: Sells from 05:30 until the market closes.

coasters.name: Madam Serwaa
coasters.text: Her pile of head pans is where every kayayo's day starts. Fair, if you're never late.
coasters.line: Load it well o. If it falls, you pay.
coasters.routine: First in the market, last to leave.

coasters.name: Maame Esi
coasters.text: The best fufu on the main road. Wash her bowls and she feeds you; work hard and she might teach you.
coasters.line: Wash these bowls and I'll give you banku.

coasters.name: Auntie Adwoa
coasters.text: Sits outside on her stool and knows everyone's business. Rent is due on Mondays.
coasters.line: Work hard o, rent is coming!
coasters.routine: On her stool by the gate, all day.

coasters.name: Mrs. Ofori
coasters.text: Forty years of teaching. She notices the children who come to school hungry.
coasters.routine: At school 07:00 to 15:00, Monday to Friday.

coasters.name: Madam Afriyie
coasters.text: Keeps the register, the fees and the certificates. Never late, never wrong.
coasters.line: Which course? Fill the form, my dear.
coasters.routine: At her desk Monday to Saturday.

coasters.name: Auntie Dede
coasters.text: Her yellow kiosk is the town's bank. She needs someone honest to mind it while she goes to the real bank.
coasters.line: Count it twice. Then count it again.
coasters.routine: At the kiosk from 07:00; to the bank by trotro at midday.

coasters.name: Pastor Mensah
coasters.text: Runs the Saturday feeding programme himself, and remembers every child's name.
coasters.line: God has a plan for you. So do I: homework.
coasters.routine: Church every day; the feeding programme on Saturdays.

coasters.name: Coach Kwesi
coasters.text: Played for a big club once, until his knee went. Now he shouts at children at six in the morning.
coasters.line: Again! The Black Stars don't rest.
coasters.routine: Training at the park at 06:00; matches on Saturdays.

coasters.name: Madam Adjoa
coasters.text: Three machines, a radio, and the neatest kaba in town. Her apprentices become masters.
coasters.line: Again. A hem must be straight like a road.

coasters.name: Kofi
coasters.text: Two years older than you and knows everything, or says he does. Your first friend.
coasters.line: Chale, follow me. I know where the bread is.

coasters.name: Uncle Bonsu
coasters.text: Decides which trotro loads next. The drivers fear him; the station boys respect him.
coasters.line: Join the queue. Everybody joins the queue.

coasters.name: Nana Kwaku Ababio II
coasters.text: Gives out the town's land and settles what the courts can't. He speaks through his linguist.
coasters.line: (Through the ɔkyeame) Nana says you are welcome.
coasters.routine: Sits at the palace in the mornings.

places.name: Nkabom Market
places.text: Tomatoes in heaps, cloth to the ceiling, the shouts of the kayayei. The heart of Gold Coast.
people: Auntie Efua, Auntie Ama, Auntie Yaa and Auntie Mansa

places.name: The rubbish heap

places.name: The traffic junction

places.name: The standpipe

places.name: Public toilet
places.text: Fifty pesewas to the attendant, who gives you a square of tissue.

places.name: Public bathhouse
places.text: A cedi for a bucket of water and a stall with a door.

places.name: Trotro station
places.text: Mates shouting destinations, benches under a shelter, and hawkers selling everything.

places.name: Maame Esi's chop bar
places.text: Fufu and light soup, waakye, banku and tilapia. Wash the bowls and she'll feed you.

places.name: Auntie Adwoa's compound house

places.text: Hymns, drums, a long sermon, and the Saturday feeding programme for the market children.

places.name: Central mosque
places.text: The call to prayer over the rooftops, and Friday's crowd in white.

places.name: Nkabom M/A Basic School

places.name: Senior high school

places.name: Sankofa Training College
places.text: Short courses that lead to work: teaching, dressmaking, mobile money.

places.name: Clinic and chemist
places.text: The nurse, the chemist, and the long bench outside. With an NHIS card it's nearly free.

places.name: Viewing centre
places.text: A big screen, plastic chairs, and the loudest room in town when the Black Stars play.

places.name: Madam Adjoa's sewing shop

places.name: Auntie Dede's MoMo kiosk

places.name: District offices

places.name: The park
places.text: A dusty field with two goalposts and no nets. The Nkabom Colts train here at dawn.

places.name: Nkabom beach
places.text: Fishing canoes painted in bright colours, nets on the sand, and the sea that gave the Gold Coast its name.

places.name: The chief's palace

jobs.title: Gold Coast today (Jobs 1 to 18)
jobs.goal: A young woman's hustle in town: walking, money on her phone, hunger and energy, the chop bar, carrying loads, rent, the college and its jobs, saving, and one shared town online.
jobs.test: 450 checks, all passing.

jobs.title: The design inside the game
jobs.goal: The game reads this design, so a change on the board changes the game.
builds: Move coaster_life.json into the game as gold-coast/data/coaster_life.json, the only copy. The board and serve.py open and save it there, and the Web export includes it (Godot leaves plain .json files out unless the export's filter names them).

Make the design match the game first: the game's tested numbers win. Her hunger and energy rates (6 and 4 an hour), the chop bar's six dishes, the loads' pay, the rent, the college's fees and the jobs' pay go into the design.
A Design autoload (autoload/design.gd) reads the file once at the start, with need(), action(), place(), step(), stage(), coaster() and lesson(). A broken file or a missing id gives a clear error.
GameState takes her need rates from the design, for her life stage, instead of its own settings.
A test loads the design, finds every id the game uses, and runs the same link checks as the board.
jobs.test: Changing hunger's young-adult rate on the board, then pressing Play, changes how fast she gets hungry; every other check still passes.
jobs.doneWhen: The game and the board share one design file, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: The tutorial: what to do now
jobs.goal: A new player always knows what to do next, and learns each thing the first time it matters.
builds: Lessons come from the design (the board's Tutorial tab): what each says, when it shows, what it points at, and what ticks it off. A lesson can show in a new game, after another lesson, when a need gets low, the first time something happens, on arriving somewhere, at a time of day, or when money goes above or below an amount.

A tip card at the top of the screen, painted like the chop bar's menu board, with the lesson's words, an icon, and the key to press. It never stops the game (only the welcome waits for a click). Doing the thing ticks it off with a little sound; 'Got it' closes it.
'Show me': the arrow from the loads (GuideMarker) points at the lesson's place, from the screen's edge when it's off screen.

Goals: a GOALS page on the phone lists what to do now, and the top one shows on the tip card when no lesson is up. They come from the tutorial now, and later from the story's chapters and the life map.
The phone's menu gains TIPS (on or off) and TUTORIAL AGAIN. Finished lessons are saved (save version 4), and a loaded game never repeats them. How to play stays, for the keys.
The first lessons, for the game as it is today: the 'New in town' lessons on the Tutorial tab.
jobs.test: A new game shows the welcome; each lesson shows once, at its moment, and ticks off when she does it; tips off hides them; saving and loading keeps them; the arrow finds each place.
jobs.doneWhen: Someone who has never played gets through the first day (earning, eating, sleeping and saving) just by following the tips.
ask: Where the tip card goes on the screen (top middle is suggested), and whether the welcome should wait for a click.

jobs.title: Water and the toilet
jobs.goal: Two new body needs, thirst and bladder, and the town's water and toilets.
builds: Thirst and bladder in GameState, like hunger and energy: rates from the design for her life stage, announced when they change, and saved.

Room on the phone for more needs: a NEEDS page (N, or the phone's left key) shows every need as a bar with its icon, and the main screen shows the two lowest instead of always food and energy. Each blinks when it's low.
A standpipe by the compound house (a new Blender prop): free water, and at times a queue of townspeople with buckets.
Pure water: the chop bar's 'pure water' fills thirst now, not hunger, and the Provisions Store sells sachets too.

A public toilet block by the market (50 pesewas, an attendant at the door) and the compound house's own toilet (free for the people who live there, with a queue in the morning). Both are new Blender models.
At 0: thirst makes her energy drain faster, and a full bladder means an accident (a text, and she needs a wash).
jobs.test: The rates match the design; drinking and the toilets fill their needs at the right prices; the accident happens at 0; saving keeps both needs.
jobs.doneWhen: She has to drink and find a toilet through the day, and the tests pass.
ask: How the needs should show on the phone, if not the two lowest on its main screen.

jobs.title: Clean and well
jobs.goal: Hygiene and health: keeping clean, getting sick, and getting better.
builds: Hygiene and health in GameState. Hygiene falls with time, and faster with hard work; health falls only through risks and events, never by the clock.
Washing: a bucket bath at home (free) and a bathhouse by the trotro station (GH₵1, a new Blender model).
Being dirty shows: sellers and customers remark on it, and the jobs that meet people pay a little less.
Getting sick: sleeping outside, mosquitoes can give her malaria (a chance, not every time). A fever slows her walk, tires her faster, and stops skilled work.
Getting better: a clinic and chemist on the main road (a new Blender model). The nurse costs more until she has an NHIS card (Job 30); the chemist is quick, but not always right.
Every risk shows its chance, like 'one time in four'.
jobs.test: Hygiene falls and baths fill it; malaria can come from mosquitoes, at its chance; a fever slows her and stops skilled work; the clinic and the chemist make her well.
jobs.doneWhen: Staying clean and well is part of her day, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Company and fun
jobs.goal: The heart needs: people to talk to, and things to enjoy.
builds: Company and fun in GameState. They count for less while she's hungry, thirsty or tired, as in the design's decision model.
Talking: E on a seller, a neighbour or a townsperson offers GREET or GIST (a short talk in Twi and Pidgin, in speech bubbles). Gisting fills company and takes a little time.
Fun: kicking the children's ball, ampe with the girls, a radio in her room, and the Black Stars at a viewing centre on match evenings (a new place).
The neighbours gist in the compound in the evenings, and she can join them.
jobs.test: Talking fills company; the games and the viewing centre fill fun; both count for less when she's hungry.
jobs.doneWhen: She has reasons to talk to people and to enjoy herself, and the tests pass.
ask: How talking should work: a short choice of lines (GREET, GIST, ASK), or one key.

jobs.title: Safe, belonging, hopeful, respected
jobs.goal: The last four needs, and the church.
builds: Safety, belonging, hope and respect in GameState. Safety falls on the street at night and fills at home; belonging grows with people who call her their own; hope with faith and small wins; respect with honest work, and it falls with shame (the gutter, begging, being late).
The Methodist church on Hill road (a new Blender model): Sunday service from 07:00 (hymns, drums, a sermon) and the Saturday feeding programme. Pastor Mensah greets everyone at the door.
Today's game feeds them: rent paid on time and loads delivered in time raise respect, a late load lowers it, and sleeping in her bed fills safety.
The NEEDS page shows all twelve, grouped as the design groups them: survival, comfort, heart, and spirit.
jobs.test: Each need moves with the right actions; the church opens on Sundays; the NEEDS page shows all twelve in their groups.
jobs.doneWhen: All twelve needs work, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Mood and moodlets
jobs.goal: How she feels: a mood from her needs and the moment, which changes how she does things.
builds: A mood from her needs (the low ones pull it down) and moodlets, the design's short feelings (Belly full, Dumsor, Chased, Black Stars won!), each lasting a while.
A small face on the phone's main screen that smiles or frowns; the NEEDS page lists the moodlets, and why.
Mood matters: in a good mood she works a little faster and gets tips; in a bad one she walks slower, and some people won't deal with her.
Moodlets from what already happens: a big meal, a payment arriving, rent paid, the room locked, mosquitoes, passing out.
jobs.test: Each moodlet starts and ends at the right time, the mood follows the needs and moodlets, and a good or bad mood changes the right things.
jobs.doneWhen: Her mood shows, explains itself, and matters, and the tests pass.
ask: How much a good or a bad mood should change things.

jobs.title: What she wants, and free will
jobs.goal: The design's decision model in the game: she can say what she wants, and look after herself.
builds: The board's simulator in GDScript: every action scored by how badly she needs what it gives, her traits and routine, and what she can't do yet, with the design's numbers.
WANTS on the phone: the three things that would help her most now, and where. The tutorial's hints use them ('She wants water: the standpipe is free').

Free will (on or off in the phone's menu): left standing for half a minute, she goes and does the top choice herself, as Sims do. Any key or click takes over, and she never undoes your choices (she won't quit a job or skip a class).
Each thing she can do in the game is tagged with its design id, so the scores know where everything is.
Traits: she gets two of the design's traits in a new game, shown on the phone.
jobs.test: WANTS match the design's scores; free will does the top choice when she's left alone; the game and the board's simulator pick the same thing from the same needs.
jobs.doneWhen: Left alone, she looks after herself sensibly, and the tests pass.
ask: Whether free will starts on or off, and whether the player picks her traits.

jobs.title: Skills that grow
jobs.goal: Skills from 0 to 10 that grow by doing, alongside the certificates.
builds: The design's fourteen skills, each from 0 to 10, growing a little each time she does something that builds them (the design's 'builds': loads build strength, the kiosk builds trading, classes build reading).
Certificates stay as education: a college course gives its certificate and also starts its skill (dressmaking starts sewing at 3).
A level up texts the phone (SEWING 4!), and a SKILLS page shows each skill's level and how far it is to the next.
Higher levels pay: a better seamstress earns more for a dress; a stronger kayayo tires less.
Skills rust slowly when they're not used, but never below what a certificate gives.
jobs.test: Doing things builds the right skills; levels show and pay; certificates set their skill; rust stops at the certificate's level.
jobs.doneWhen: You can watch her get better at things by doing them, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: People who know you
jobs.goal: Relationships: the people of Gold Coast remember her, from stranger to family.
builds: The design's named Coasters each know her somewhere on the ladder: stranger, familiar face, padi (friend), trusted, family. Their personalities and lines come from the design.
It grows with greeting, gisting, helping, working for them and paying on time, and falls with lateness, quarrels and unpaid rent (it builds on Job 23's talking).
CONTACTS on the phone, like an old Nokia's phonebook: each person, where to find them, and how well they know her.
Each rung changes something: Madam Serwaa gives better-paid loads to someone she trusts, Maame Esi adds a little extra for a padi, and Auntie Adwoa waits a day for the rent of someone trusted.
jobs.test: Each action moves the right person the right way; every rung's change works; contacts are saved.
jobs.doneWhen: The people she deals with remember her and treat her differently, and the tests pass.
ask: What each of the six people should give at each rung.

jobs.title: A good name, and achievements
jobs.goal: Reputation in each circle of the town, and milestones the game celebrates.
builds: Reputation in the design's six circles (the market, the street, church or mosque, school, the family, the town), each from 0 to 100, moved by what she does: loads in time raise the market's, honest change raises it more, a late load lowers it.
The design's achievements, noticed by the game (First cedi, Honest with money, First susu payout…), each with a jingle and a text. A NAME page on the phone shows her reputation and achievements.
A test of honesty now and then: a customer pays too much, and she can give back the change.
Reputation and achievements count towards the life map's steps (Job 31).
jobs.test: Each action moves the right circle; each achievement fires once, at the right moment; both are saved.
jobs.doneWhen: Her good name grows with honest work, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Papers, and the district offices
jobs.goal: Documents as things she has: a birth certificate, an NHIS card and a Ghana Card, and later a licence and a passport.
builds: Papers among her things, on a PAPERS page: the 'New in town' start has a birth certificate and a Ghana Card, and she can get an NHIS card.
The district offices in the old town (a new Blender model): the registry, the NIA and the NHIS desk, with a queue that starts at dawn.
Queues take time, and some days 'the network is down: come back tomorrow'.
The NHIS card makes the nurse cheap (Job 22). Papers will open other steps later: a Ghana Card for a SIM and a wallet of her own (Job 41).
jobs.test: Papers come the right way; the queue and its bad days work; the NHIS card changes the clinic's price; papers are saved.
jobs.doneWhen: She can get her papers, and they matter, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: The life map in the game
jobs.goal: Her phone shows what she can become next, and exactly what each step needs.
builds: Checkable requirements: on the board's step form, each line of 'What it takes' can say how the game checks it (a skill and a level, a person and a rung, a circle and a level, a paper, a step done, an achievement, money, or a choice). Lines without one are shown, but not checked.
A LIFE page on the phone: the steps she can reach next, each line ticked or not ('every lock says how to open it'), and 'Show me' to point the way.
A step happens when all its lines are ticked and its moment comes (paying the fee, a ceremony, a talk): a fanfare, a text, and the new things it opens.
A big map view, like the board's, with the steps she's done lit up.
Steps done are saved, and each start begins with its own already done (for 'New in town': a birth certificate, a Ghana Card, a wallet, carrying loads, and a rented room).
jobs.test: Every step's lines check correctly; steps happen when they should and never before; no step opens with money alone.
jobs.doneWhen: You can plan her life from the phone, and the tests pass.
ask: Whether the big map opens on the phone or on its own screen.

jobs.title: Choices
jobs.goal: Moments where the player decides, which the life map remembers.
builds: A choice card: a question, two or three answers, and what each costs or opens. It comes when the story or a step needs it (school or a full day's work; the easy money or not).
Choices live in the design: a new 'choices' list, with its own section on the board, each with when it comes, its answers, and what they change.
Choices made are saved, and the life map's 'choice' lines check them.
The first ones, for the young woman: give back extra change, lend money to a friend, join the market susu or not.
jobs.test: Each choice comes at its moment; its answers change the right things; the life map sees them.
jobs.doneWhen: Her choices shape what she can become, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: The week, the weather, and dumsor
jobs.goal: The town's rhythms: days that differ, seasons, rain and power cuts.
builds: Days of the week matter: Sunday church, the Saturday feeding programme, Friday prayers at the central mosque in the zongo (a new place), and market days on Tuesday and Friday (more loads, more customers).

Months and seasons: the Harmattan (December to February: dry haze, and thirst falls faster) and the rains (April to July: showers, flooded gutters, more mosquitoes). Rain uses Job 11's lighting presets, or brings them forward.
Dumsor: some evenings the power cuts out. The street lamps and the kiosk's light go dark, the viewing centre closes, and the 'Dumsor' moodlet starts.
Month end: salaries, queues at the MoMo kiosk, and the susu paying out.
Online, everyone in the shared town has the same weather and power cuts, as they have the same clock.
jobs.test: Each day, season and power cut comes when it should, and changes the right things.
jobs.doneWhen: The town feels different on a Sunday, in the rain, and in a power cut, and the tests pass.
ask: How often dumsor should come, and how long the rains should last.

jobs.title: Street events
jobs.goal: Surprises with choices: the design's street events in the game.
builds: An event card, like the choice card: what's happening, and the answers. There's always a safe way out that costs something, and chancier ones with their odds shown (Street smarts: 70%), or ones that need a person, a paper or a skill.
Events start by place, time, life stage and chance, never too often.
The first ones: the city guards at the junction, a kind stranger, touts at the station, the susu collector vanishing, and a funeral on Saturday.
Their odds use her skills (Job 27) and the people she knows (Job 28).
jobs.test: Each event starts only where and when it should; its odds follow her skills; every answer does what it says.
jobs.doneWhen: The town surprises her, with real choices, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Townspeople who live by their needs
jobs.goal: The people of Gold Coast are Coasters too, with needs, personalities and routines from the design.
builds: The named Coasters follow their routines from the design (Maame Esi pounds fufu from 10:00, Auntie Dede goes to the bank at midday) instead of fixed scripts.
Some townspeople choose what to do with the decision model (Job 26): a hungry one goes to the chop bar, a tired one goes home.
Far from her, people only count their needs roughly and move between places, like the towns in The Sims, so the game stays fast on the web.
Each named Coaster has their own traits from the design, which show in what they do and say. Uncle Bonsu, the station master, comes to the trotro station.
jobs.test: Routines run on time from the design; hungry townspeople eat; the frame rate holds 60 on the web.
jobs.doneWhen: The town runs on the same rules she does, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Growing up: life stages
jobs.goal: Age and the six life stages: what changes as a Coaster grows, and how the years pass.
builds: Age and life stage in GameState and the save. Each stage takes its numbers from the design: how fast needs fall, what she can do, how fast she walks, and her size.

How the years pass: a chapter ends when its goals are done (or after enough days). A 'Two years later…' card sums up what happened, then the next chapter starts. Needs, skills, people and papers carry over.

What she carries by stage: a toddler or a child has coins in a pocket, not a phone, so the needs and goals show on a small tin box instead. The phone comes with her first one (a step on the life map).
The 'New in town' start (today's game) is a young adult, so nothing changes for it.
Online, the town shows other players at their own ages, and a time skip happens only for the player who skips.
jobs.test: Each stage's numbers come from the design; a chapter's end moves her on with everything carried over; the HUD follows her stage.
jobs.doneWhen: A Coaster can grow from one stage to the next, and the tests pass.
ask: How long a chapter should last if its goals aren't done.

jobs.title: A toddler, a child and a teen
jobs.goal: Her younger selves, built in Blender the same way as the young woman.
builds: build_player_character.py makes her at three younger ages: a toddler in an old, too-big T-shirt, a girl in school uniform (and in play clothes), and a teen in a kaba and slit, in the same style and colors.
The animations they need: toddling, sitting on a sack, sleeping curled up, carrying a small bowl, and playing. The teen carries a head pan like the woman.
The town's children use them too, so the market children look like hers.
Pictures of each from every side, like the woman's preview.
jobs.test: Each model loads with its animations, matches the style, and stays light enough for the web.
jobs.doneWhen: You can see her at every age, and the tests pass.
ask: What she wears at each age (drawings welcome, as for the trotro).

jobs.title: Chapter 1: The market raised me
jobs.goal: A new start: a three-year-old alone at Nkabom Market, and the first chapter of her life.
builds: NEW GAME asks where to start: 'Alone at the market' (a toddler) or 'New in town' (the young woman, as now).

The market child's world: the rubbish heap behind the market, a junction where the traffic stops, Auntie Akos's kenkey stall and Mama Akua's tomatoes (new sellers), Kofi the market boy, and the church's Saturday feeding programme.

Her actions: picking food from the rubbish (with its risk), helping a seller carry her bowls, sitting by a stall, splashing at the standpipe, begging at the junction, napping in the shade, and sleeping under a market table.
The chapter's goals on the tin box (a kind kenkey seller, a safe place to sleep, the feeding programme), its story beats as short picture cards, and its end: 'Two years later…', into Chapter 2.
The market child's tutorial lessons (the Tutorial tab).
jobs.test: A toddler game starts at the market; every goal can be reached by following the tips; the chapter ends into the child stage.
jobs.doneWhen: You can play the market child's first chapter from start to end, and the tests pass.
ask: Whether the toddler is always a girl, like the young woman, or the player chooses.

jobs.title: Chapter 2: A name on paper
jobs.goal: The child years: a home, a birth certificate, school, and the first cedis.
builds: Taken in by Auntie Akos: a mat in her room at the compound house, chores in the morning, and her children as brothers and sisters.
The birth certificate at the registry (Job 30's district offices), with Auntie Akos swearing for her.
Nkabom M/A Basic School as a pupil: classes on weekdays (on the school's benches, with Mrs. Ofori), homework under the street light, and the headmistress's scholarship call.
Work for a child: hawking pure water at the junction, calling passengers at the station, errands for the compound, and washing bowls at Maame Esi's.
Play: football at the park, where the colts coach watches, and the children's choir.
The chapter's goals, beats and tutorial lessons, and its end into the teen years.
jobs.test: Every goal of the chapter can be reached; school days and work fit around each other; the chapter ends into the teen stage.
jobs.doneWhen: You can play the child's chapter from start to end, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Chapter 3: The head pan
jobs.goal: The teen years: carrying loads, the BECE, and the big choice of school, a trade, or the street.
builds: Carrying loads as a teen kayayo (today's loads, from Job 8), with a head pan bought from Madam Serwaa's pile.
The market susu: a cedi a day to the collector, and the payout at the month's end (and the risk he vanishes, Job 34).
The BECE at the end of JHS 3, and its results day.

The choice of paths: a Free SHS place (boarding school away from town, told as a time skip with letters home), an apprenticeship with Madam Adjoa (a new sewing shop on Market road), or the station boys.
The colts club and the youth fellowship, for the players who choose them.
The chapter's goals, beats and tutorial lessons, and its end into the young adult years.
jobs.test: Each path can be chosen and played; the susu pays out; the chapter ends into the young adult stage with the right steps done.
jobs.doneWhen: You can play the teen's chapter on each path, and the tests pass.
ask: Whether SHS is a time skip, or a school she can play at.

jobs.title: Chapter 4: Freedom
jobs.goal: The young adult years, joining today's game: papers, a phone of her own, a trade, and love.
builds: The market child, grown up, reaches where the 'New in town' start begins: loads, a rented room at Auntie Adwoa's, and the college. From here both starts share the chapter.
The freedom ceremony for an apprentice (drinks, prayers and a certificate in front of both families), and sewing for the market women.
Her own phone and mobile money wallet, with her Ghana Card (Job 30): until now the phone wasn't hers.
Courtship and the knocking ceremony: someone who walks her home after church.
The trotro mate's job, a driver's licence, and driving a trotro. The WASSCE for the ones who went to SHS.
The chapter's goals, beats and tutorial lessons. Chapters 5 and 6 (an adult and an elder) come later.
jobs.test: Both starts reach this chapter with the right steps done, and each of its goals can be reached.
jobs.doneWhen: The story runs from the market toddler to a young woman with a trade, and the tests pass.

jobs.title: Later: an adult, an elder, and more starts
jobs.goal: To plan once Chapter 4 plays well.
builds: Chapter 5, 'Block by block' (an adult): a stall of her own, a chop bar, land and landguards, building a house, marriage, a child, the market queen and the Assembly.
Chapter 6, 'Sankofa' (an elder): the family head, feeding the market children, a will, and playing on as her child.
The other starts: the fisher's child (with the beach and its canoes), sent to town, and the compound family.
More paths: university and National Service, the colts' academy trial, Uber, the MoMo agent's own kiosk, and the abroad dream.

tutorial.title: Akwaaba!
tutorial.text: This is you: new in Gold Coast, with GH₵100 on your phone. Walk with WASD or the arrow keys, or click where you want to go.

tutorial.title: Your phone
tutorial.text: Your phone shows your money, the time and the day. The bars down its sides are your food and energy: when one blinks, see to it.

tutorial.title: Earn your first cedis
tutorial.text: Madam Serwaa at Nkabom Market pays kayayei to carry loads. Press E at her stall to take one.

tutorial.title: Carry it there
tutorial.text: Follow the arrow to the gold ring, and press E to hand the load over. In time, full pay; late, half.

tutorial.title: Paid by mobile money
tutorial.text: The money came to your phone, with a text. Every payment in and out shows there.

tutorial.title: Hungry?
tutorial.text: Maame Esi's chop bar sells food. Walk up to her stall, press E, and pick what you can afford.

tutorial.title: Short of money?
tutorial.text: Maame Esi pays GH₵20 to wash her bowls, once a day. Press E at the basin by her stall.

tutorial.title: Tired?
tutorial.text: Sleep in your room at Auntie Adwoa's compound house: press E at the door. You can sleep on the street with Z, but mosquitoes will wake you.

tutorial.title: Your day is saved
tutorial.text: Going to bed saves the game. You can also save whenever you're free, from the phone's menu (M).

tutorial.title: Night is coming
tutorial.text: The market closed at 18:00, and the street gets dark. Get home to your bed.

tutorial.title: Rent is coming
tutorial.text: Auntie Adwoa wants GH₵140 every Monday at 08:00. If you can't pay, she locks your room until you do.

tutorial.title: A way up
tutorial.text: Carrying loads is hard work. Sankofa Training College teaches skills that pay more: see Madam Afriyie at her desk.

tutorial.title: Thirsty?
tutorial.text: The standpipe by the compound house is free. A sachet of pure water is 50 pesewas at the chop bar or the store.

tutorial.title: Need the toilet?
tutorial.text: The public toilet by the market is 50 pesewas. The compound house has one for the people who live there.

tutorial.title: All your needs
tutorial.text: Press N to see all your needs. The phone's screen shows the two lowest.

tutorial.title: Time for a wash
tutorial.text: A bucket bath at home is free, and the bathhouse by the station is GH₵1. People notice when you need one.

tutorial.title: A fever
tutorial.text: It's malaria. See the nurse at the clinic, or buy tablets at the chemist. Sleeping outside brings the mosquitoes.

tutorial.title: Lonely?
tutorial.text: Press E on a neighbour or a seller to greet them, or gist. People are good company.

tutorial.title: Sunday
tutorial.text: On Sundays the Methodist church on Hill road fills with songs. It's good for hope, and for meeting people.

tutorial.title: How you feel
tutorial.text: The face on your phone shows your mood. The NEEDS page says why.

tutorial.title: Not sure what to do?
tutorial.text: The phone's WANTS show the three things that would help most right now, and where to find them.

tutorial.title: Getting better
tutorial.text: Doing things builds skills. The SKILLS page shows how far you've got, and better skills pay more.

tutorial.title: People remember
tutorial.text: Your CONTACTS show who knows you, and how well. People treat a padi better than a stranger.

tutorial.title: An achievement!
tutorial.text: The game noticed. Your achievements and your good name, on the NAME page, help open new steps in life.

tutorial.title: Papers
tutorial.text: The district offices make the papers that open doors: an NHIS card for cheap visits to the nurse, and a Ghana Card. The queue starts at dawn.

tutorial.title: What can you become?
tutorial.text: Your phone's LIFE page shows the steps you can reach next, and exactly what each one needs. Money alone never opens one.

tutorial.title: Your choice
tutorial.text: Some moments ask you to decide. What you choose stays with you, and opens different steps in life.

tutorial.title: Something's happening
tutorial.text: There's always a safe way out that costs something, and chancier ways. The odds show beside each one.

tutorial.title: You're three
tutorial.text: Your mother is gone, and the market is your home now. Walk with WASD, or click where you want to go.

tutorial.title: Your tin box
tutorial.text: Your tin box shows your needs, the coins in your pocket, and what to do now. Hunger and thirst come fast when you're small.

tutorial.title: Your goals
tutorial.text: These are this chapter's goals. Reach them all, and the years move on.

tutorial.title: Find food
tutorial.text: The rubbish heap behind the market has leftovers: free, but they can make you sick. Helping a seller carry her bowls earns a little kenkey.

tutorial.title: Water
tutorial.text: The standpipe is free. Cup your hands under the tap.

tutorial.title: Need to go?
tutorial.text: The public toilet costs 50 pesewas that you don't have. The gutter is free, but people see.

tutorial.title: Auntie Akos
tutorial.text: The kenkey seller watches you. Help her carry her bowls five days in a row, and she'll remember you.

tutorial.title: Night
tutorial.text: The market empties at night. Sleep under a market table. Mama Akua's is the safest, once she knows you.

tutorial.title: Saturday
tutorial.text: On Saturday mornings the church feeds the market children. Follow them up Hill road.
